data.name: GADD45alpha
data.description: Stress-inducible DNA repair protein regulated downstream of the mTOR-TFEB axis. Astragaloside IV reactivated TFEB by inhibiting mTOR, which restored GADD45alpha expression along with renal function, pathology, autophagic flux and DNA repair in a mouse model of tacrolimus nephrotoxicity; the effects were reversed by TFEB knockdown (GAO2026, PMID 42438242). Mouse in vivo plus cell work, not a human finding.
data.description_beginner: A stress-response, DNA-repair protein controlled downstream of the mTOR-TFEB signaling chain. Restoring its levels - by activating TFEB - has helped protect against drug-induced kidney damage in animal studies.

studies.title: Astragaloside IV Mitigates Tacrolimus-Induced Chronic Nephrotoxicity by Regulating the mTOR-TFEB-GADD45α Pathway.
studies.authors: Gao P; Cheng X; Xu R; Huang X; Wang J; Liu M; Wu X; Guan X; Chen Y; Qiu Z
studies.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse (tacrolimus-induced chronic nephrotoxicity model) + renal cell lines
studies.finding: Astragaloside IV protects against tacrolimus-induced nephrotoxicity by inhibiting mTOR to activate TFEB and restore autophagy, nominating the mTOR-TFEB-GADD45alpha axis as a calcineurin-independent candidate therapeutic target (preclinical; no human data) in TICN.
